messages:
Carla: Quick follow-up on the delta quant ladder RFC — we sketched FP8 -> INT8 -> 4bit ladder for cost-sensitive tenants. Two quick questions: 1) how should runtime signal quality regressions to trigger rollback vs fallback? 2) what's the minimal shim to make Dedicated/Private adopt the same profile?

Ben: For signals, I prefer a combo: per-endpoint task metric (BLEU/QA F1 or whatever the customer uses) + token-level perplexity drift + hard error-rate (bad completions). We already emit a per-request 'deg_score' metric — can we reuse that? :thinking:

Alice: We can reuse deg_score but it needs calibration per-profile. Suggest adding 'deg_thresholds' into profile metadata, e.g.:
```
quant_profile: delta-ladder-v1
deg_thresholds: {fp8: 0.08, int8: 0.05, 4bit: 0.02}
fallback_policy: {graceful: true, fallback_variant: "int8-safe"}
```
Then runtime compares rolling 5m avg against those thresholds before triggering fallback.

David: Implementation note: runtime shouldn't hard-rollback model on first sign of trouble. Do graceful fallback first (route to compatible safer variant) and then trigger alert/ops escalation. Also need a consistent API between hosted / dedicated / private — plan: expose a small gRPC control plane on the private agent that accepts profile updates and exposes health hooks.

Carla: Agree on graceful fallback. For canaries: propose a rollout CLI like `rictl rollout --profile delta-ladder-v1 --canary 3% --stability 10m` (canary percent + observed window). Add a safety net to auto-bump to int8 if fp8 deg_score > threshold for N consecutive requests.

Ben: Edge-case: long-context prompts amplify FP8 artifacts. We should gate fp8 for sequence_len > 2048 or apply per-layer FP8 disable. Maybe store `max_context_fp8` and `per_layer_fp8_blacklist` in the profile.

Alice: Perf/engine note: switching mid-request is messy because KV cache encoding/layout can differ between variants. Two options: 1) require model variants to share compatible KV layout (preferred), or 2) force a full KV cache reset on fallback and accept a latency spike. I vote for the compatibility constraint + an explicit compatibility flag in the profile.

David: On Dedicated/Private: customers will want an opt-out and predictable behavior. Add profile opt-in per-deployment and a `profile_compatibility_check` that runs a small local eval suite before enabling a profile. Also we should document the minimal shim: a one-file JSON profile and a one-endpoint gRPC call to apply it.

ops-bot: Created RFC follow-up PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/254 — added metadata suggestions and rollout CLI. CI tests scheduled.

Carla: Action items: Ben to prototype deg_threshold calibration script + perf sweep, Alice to write up profile metadata + KV compatibility rules, David to draft private agent gRPC interface and compatibility check. Ping me when the PR is ready. :thumbsup:
